archetype.name: Gunslinger
archetype.definition: A big-armed veteran who hunts air yards, lives with turnovers and sacks as the cost of doing business, and wins games when the deep ball connects more often than the intermediate throws get picked.

report.headline: Same Jameis: deep shots pay, short game sputters, and the turnovers are coming
report.take:
Winston took over a Giants offense that Jaxson Dart started in Weeks 1 and 2. He played 88% of snaps in that Week 2 loss to the Rams and has started the last two. The profile is the one he has carried for a decade. His 21.8% aggressiveness, 2.78-second time to throw and 9.3 intended air yards sit right on his 2016-2019 marks of about 17-22% aggressiveness and 2.77-2.88 seconds. His 15.4% bad-throw rate is actually better than most of his career seasons. Nothing about how he plays has changed. What changed is the setting: a John Harbaugh team that passes 10 points below expectation (31st) behind a line allowing hits at the 30th-worst rate.

The split by depth explains the season. On 12 deep attempts he has +1.03 EPA per play and +14.5 CPOE. That is the reason a gunslinger exists, and it is carrying almost all of his value. Everything underneath has been poor. Throws behind the line are at -0.56 EPA. Throws of 0-9 yards are at -0.32 with a -19.8 CPOE, which is hard to do at that depth. The intermediate band has produced 2 TDs and all 3 interceptions on 19 throws. Isaiah Likely has drawn a team-high 26 targets at -0.25 EPA per target. So the most-fed option is where drives go to die, while Darnell Mooney (+0.37) and Cam Skattebo (+0.28) have been efficient on small volume.

The -0.215 EPA per dropback (37th of 42) looks worse than the trajectory. His game EPA went -16.5, then -6.1, then +3.9, while the opponents went from the 4th-ranked defense to the 21st to the 28th. The Rams game was a relief appearance against a top-five unit. The 36-24 win over Arizona showed the full package: 250 yards, 3 TDs, 2 INTs and 4 sacks. The 10.3% sack rate is part line and part him. His 31.3% pressure-to-sack rate matches his career band of roughly 27-34%.

Going forward, expect volatility rather than steady improvement. The deep efficiency will cool on a bigger sample. The short-area accuracy should rise toward his career-normal CPOE, which has hovered near zero, because -19.8 underneath is an outlier even for him. The interceptions are structural. A run-first coach caps his volume, so this is an offense he can keep afloat, not one he will carry.

strengths.title: Deep ball is producing real points
strengths.body: On 20+ air-yard throws he is hitting half his attempts, at +14.5 CPOE and over a point of EPA per play. That is the whole case for playing him. Twelve attempts is a small sample and it will cool. Still, his career aggressiveness and air-yard numbers say he will keep taking these shots, and the payoff has historically come with them.

strengths.title: Trending up as opponents softened
strengths.body: His EPA climbed in every game: -16.5, then -6.1, then +3.9. The Arizona game was the first time he looked like a functional starter, with 3 TDs and 250 yards. Part of that is the opponent getting easier, but it also came with a full week of starter preparation after a relief debut.

strengths.title: Better when under center
strengths.body: On 18 under-center dropbacks he is at +0.23 EPA with a 50% success rate. Shotgun has been -0.33. This fits a Harbaugh offense built on play-action and the run. It is a small sample, but it points to a usage that hides his underneath accuracy problems.

concerns.title: Intermediate throws are the turnover zone
concerns.body: All three of his interceptions came on 10-19 yard throws, where he is completing 42% of 19 attempts. That has been his signature flaw for years, from 30 interceptions in 2019 to a bottom-quartile interception rank in 2024. It is the cost of his aggressiveness, not bad luck, so expect roughly one interception a game to hold.

concerns.title: Short game accuracy is broken
concerns.body: A -19.8 CPOE on 0-9 yard throws, and -0.56 EPA on throws behind the line, means the easy completions are not happening. That kills third downs, where he converts 30.3% while facing an average of 9.5 yards to go. His career CPOE has mostly been near average, so some recovery is likely. Until it comes, drives stall.

concerns.title: Sacks: shared blame with the line
concerns.body: His 10.3% sack rate ranks 38th of 42. The Giants allow hits at the 30th-worst rate, so the protection is genuinely poor. His pressure-to-sack rate is also in line with his career norm, which means he holds the ball hunting downfield. This will persist with this line.

trend.note: His per-game EPA improved each week, from -16.5 to -6.1 to +3.9. The opponent's defensive rank also softened each week, from 4th to 21st to 28th, so part of the climb is schedule.

nextGame.headline: Washington's leaky deep coverage meets Winston's best throw
nextGame.body:
Washington's defense is built almost exactly wrong for him. It is stingy underneath, allowing -0.12 EPA on short throws (5th), which is precisely where Winston has been broken. But it bleeds deep, allowing +1.08 EPA on deep throws (26th), and Winston's deep passing is the one thing working. Washington allows 22.5 PPR points and 3 TDs per game to quarterbacks, both near the bottom of the league. Its 4.6% sack rate (23rd) is a lighter pass rush than he has faced, which should cut into his sack problem. The underneath stinginess may force him into more intermediate throws, his interception zone, so this is a high-variance setup rather than a clean one.

Availability tilts toward the deep game. Starting safety Nick Cross (99% of snaps) is out. Jeremy Reaves (91%) is questionable with a finger injury, and backup safety Tyler Owens is questionable with a hamstring. A thin back end is exactly what a vertical thrower wants. Edge Charles Omenihu is questionable with a groin injury, which could thin the rush further. On the other side, Washington's QB is unsettled. Jayden Daniels is listed out with a dislocated elbow, though the coaching staff is aiming for him to start. Mariota is doubtful, McLaurin is out, and guard Sam Cosmi is out. A diminished Washington offense keeps the game closer and Winston's script more balanced. On the Giants' side, only Braxton Berrios (9% of snaps) is on the report, which changes nothing.

keyMatchups.title: Winston deep vs depleted safeties
keyMatchups.body: Washington's deep defense ranks 26th and its starting safety Cross is out, with Reaves questionable. Winston's 12 deep attempts have been his most efficient throws by far. If the Giants use play-action from under center to set up shots, this is where the game is decided.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into a stingy underneath
keyMatchups.body: Washington allows only -0.12 EPA on short throws (5th). That plays into Winston's worst area, his 0-9 yard accuracy. Expect checkdowns to Likely to keep failing and the offense to lean on chunk plays.

keyMatchups.title: A lighter rush than he's seen
keyMatchups.body: Washington's 4.6% sack rate ranks 23rd, and Omenihu is questionable. Fewer free rushers means more time for Winston's 2.8-second deep drops. That should push his sack rate back toward his career norm.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Giants call play-action shots from under center early. That is how they put his deep ball on Washington's depleted safeties instead of asking him to dink against a top-five short defense.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a volatile, roughly league-average-minus starter. Games like Arizona will be mixed with clunkers against good defenses. The +1.03 deep EPA will regress on volume. The -19.8 CPOE on short throws should also regress, upward, toward his near-zero career baseline, so the two should partly offset. Interceptions near one per game are a career constant and will not go away. The sack rate should ease a little but stay high behind a line allowing hits at a bottom-three rate.

The ceiling is capped by Harbaugh's run-first approach: a pass rate 10 points under expectation means few 40-attempt shootouts. One more factor is outside the dossier's view. Dart started the first two weeks, so the hold on the job depends on Winston's turnovers not outweighing his big plays.
swingFactors: Short-area accuracy normalizing toward his career CPOE
Pass protection, given a bottom-three hit rate allowed
Job security against Jaxson Dart if turnovers pile up

bets.reason: His season average is dragged down by a partial relief game. Washington allows 270.8 passing yards a game to quarterbacks (23rd) and ranks 26th in deep EPA allowed, with safety Cross out. The Giants' run-heavy rate caps the upside, but he cleared 250 as a full starter against a soft defense.
Washington allows 3 QB touchdowns per game (31st). Winston's deep shots and red-zone work have produced 3 TDs in his two starts.

He has 3 interceptions on 78 attempts, all on intermediate throws. Washington's stingy short defense pushes him into exactly that range. Over his career he has rarely held interceptions below roughly one per game.

Washington's quarterback is unsettled: Daniels is coming off a dislocated elbow, Mariota is doubtful, McLaurin and guard Cosmi are out. Its offense already ranks 29th in success rate, and its defense ranks 19th, close to the Giants' 20th. Three points for a road underdog in a division game looks generous.

confidence.note: 89 dropbacks across 2.5 games, including a relief appearance, and the opposing QB situation is unsettled.
